old_claim: The 09:45 theorem transfers bounded source LDA to positive read-k local-union tests using aggregate spectral dimension, but still needs union positivity/read-k structure for its strong-test conclusion.
new_claim: For any signed local score F=sum_j a_j h_j under a uniform product reference, bounded source LDA through D implies noisy normalized advantage at most A+sqrt(s_F/kappa_F), where kappa_F is the actual coefficient-direction Rayleigh quotient of the local correlation Gram matrix and s_F is the effective normalized local high-degree spectral tail. This removes read-k, positivity, rarity, monotonicity and disjointness for the signed polynomial class.
proof_mechanism: Project T_rho F once at source degree D. LDA controls the low projection. Unit-modulus Walsh characters control each local high-degree residual in sup norm. The variance identity Var(F)=b^T Gamma b converts the result into an explicit forward frame/correlation Rayleigh quotient, avoiding signed inverse-Gram geometry.
strictness_example: Distinct overlapping parity characters have Gamma=I regardless of arbitrarily large coordinate read number; with width w>D and log m=o(w), their residual term sqrt(m) rho^w vanishes.
mao_boundary: Since Mao has A=0 through D_n, any successful signed-local representation must satisfy s_F/kappa_F >= Delta_F^2. Thus a Mao-type escape must exhibit frame collapse or persistent local source-high-degree spectral mass (or fail to admit the representation).
exact_gap: Arbitrary S_n-invariant graph polynomials and general polynomial-time tests need not admit a polynomial-size local decomposition with a noncollapsing correlation frame and small local residual. Orbit-size amplification remains uncontrolled.
next_attack: Compress S_n-invariant graph polynomials into graph-shape orbit pieces and seek an orbit-normalized residual bound that avoids paying labeled orbit size. If that fails, pivot to noisy branching-program Fourier concentration robustified from exact bounded independence to bounded LDA.
